issue.title: `read_file` pagination skips lines after wrapping due to double limit application
issue.body:
### Checked other resources

- [x] This is a bug, not a usage question.
- [x] I added a clear and descriptive title.
- [x] I searched existing issues and didn't find this.
- [x] I can reproduce this with the latest released version.
- [x] I included a minimal reproducible example and steps to reproduce.

### Area (Required)

- [x] deepagents (SDK)
- [ ] cli

### Related Issues / PRs

_No response_

### Reproduction Steps / Example Code (Python)

```python
from deepagents import create_deep_agent
from deepagents.backends.state import StateBackend
from deepagents.utils import prepopulate_file
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage

# Create a file with one very long line
backend = StateBackend()
file_path = "/wrapped.txt"

long_line = "x" * 15000
content = "\n".join([
    "line1",
    long_line,
    "important instruction",
    "line4",
])

files = prepopulate_file(backend, file_path, content)

agent = create_deep_agent(backend=backend)

# Read first page
result1 = agent.invoke({
    "messages": [HumanMessage(content=f"read {file_path} with offset=0 limit=3")],
    "files": files
})

# Read second page
result2 = agent.invoke({
    "messages": [HumanMessage(content=f"read {file_path} with offset=3 limit=3")]
})

print(result1)
print(result2)
```

### Error Message and Stack Trace (if applicable)

```shell

```

### Description

read_file can skip lines when paginating a file that contains very long lines.

If a long line is wrapped into multiple display rows, only part of the formatted output may be returned, even though the backend already fetched the next line. When the next page is requested, pagination continues from a later offset, so the skipped line is never shown.

Expected: all fetched lines should always appear across pages.
Actual: some lines are skipped when wrapping occurs.

### Environment / System Info

OS: Windows
Python: 3.12.4
deepagents: 0.5.0a3

steps: Create /home/agent/workspace/wrapped.txt containing four LF-separated lines: line1; then exactly 15000 lowercase x characters; then important instruction; then line4. Use the normal file tools or shell to create these exact contents.
expected: The two read pages include every requested source line, including important instruction.
defect: Formatting a long line wraps it into display rows and applies the page limit again, dropping an already-fetched source line.

fault location.explanation: The backend slices source lines first; the filesystem middleware then reapplies limit to the wrapped rendered rows. The next offset advances past source content that was never emitted. #3641 removes the second limiting step.

Root cause: The backend slices source lines first; the filesystem middleware then reapplies limit to the wrapped rendered rows. The next offset advances past source content that was never emitted. #3641 removes the second limiting step.
